summary: Beiho Takashima (1875–1949) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Toyo University (~1897–1900). He founded the Bukkyo Seito Doshikai and held a post at Toyo University (~1926–1931).

Beiyin Deng works in Buddhist and religious studies, holding degrees from Fudan University, New York University, and Arizona State University (Ph.D. 2024). Deng served as a Visiting Instructor at Grinnell College and became Assistant Professor at the University of Missouri in 2024.

Bela Bhattacharya (b. 1950) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She served as Professor in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011) and held a professorship at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Beligalle Dhammajoti is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. from Banaras Hindu University. He has served as a Professor at the University of Ruhuna and as Venerable Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Bemé Shyi Drol was a scholar who studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Ben Jiao is a Tibetologist who completed a Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University in 2001 under Melvyn C. Goldstein. He served as Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2008).
Ben Joffe is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Colorado Boulder under the supervision of Carole McGranahan (attested 2019).

Benedetta Lomi earned a PhD from SOAS University of London (~2006–2011). A scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, she held posts at UC Berkeley and the University of Virginia before becoming Senior Lecturer at the University of Bristol.
Benhua Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a doctoral degree from Nanjing University (2018–2021). Yang holds a post at Anhui University.

Benigno Ferrario (1887–1956) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale." He served as Professor of Classical Languages and Philosophy at the University of the Republic.

Benimadhab Barua (1888–1948) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Presidency University, the University of Calcutta, and the University of London (D.Litt.). He served as headmaster at Mahamuni Anglo-Pali Institution and as Professor at the University of Calcutta (1918–1948).

Benjamin A. Elman (b. 1946) is a sinologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He held major posts at UCLA (1986–2002) and Princeton University (beginning 2002).
Benjamin Bogin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2006) under Donald S. Lopez Jr.

Benjamin Brose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his Ph.D. from Stanford University (~2003–2009) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure. He was an assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan (~2010–2017).

Benjamin C. Ray (b. 1940) is a religious studies scholar who has served on the faculty at the University of Virginia, including as the Daniels Family NEH Distinguished Teaching Professor in the Department of Religious Studies (attested 2000, 2026).
Benjamin Fleming is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from McMaster University and held a post at the City University of New York (attested 2021).

Benjamin Fürchtegott Balthasar von Bergmann (1772–1856) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Leipzig and Jena before completing his Ph.D. at the University of Tartu in 1816.
Benjamin Goldstein is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke (attested 2026).

Benjamin Guy Babington (1794–1866) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the East India Company College, Guy's Hospital, and the University of Cambridge. He co-founded the Madras Literary Society and served as physician at Guy's Hospital (~1837–1855).

Benjamin H. Rice (1814–1887) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Homerton College from 1834 to 1836. He served as a teacher and missionary for the London Missionary Society beginning in 1836.
